programme.title: The Promised Land
programme.desc: In 1755, the poor soldier Ludvig Kahlen arrives on the barren Jutland moors with a single goal: to follow the king's call to cultivate the land and gain wealth and honour for himself. However, the ruthless landowner, Frederik De Schinkel, believes the moor belongs to him.

programme.title: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
programme.desc: Richard E Grant follows in the footsteps of artists who have lived, loved and painted on France's Cote d'Azur. Revealing the intertwined relationship between modern art and the development of the French Riviera as an international tourist haven, Grant explores how Impressionist painters Cezanne, Monet and Renoir first discovered the region in the 19th century when the newly-built railway arrived there.

programme.title: Scotland: Rome's Final Frontier
programme.desc: Were the ancient Scottish tribes too much for the Roman Empire? Or was Scotland simply not worth conquering? Archaeologist Dr Fraser Hunter looks back on three centuries of contact and conflict with the Roman invaders. Features the first Tay Bridge, the first depiction of tartan, and forgotten Roman camps that once held thirty-five thousand men.

programme.title: Tutankhamun: The Truth Uncovered
programme.desc: What killed King Tutankhamun? Ever since his spectacular tomb was discovered, the boy king has been the most famous pharaoh of all ancient Egypt. But his mysterious death, at just 19 years old, has never been explained. In this BBC One special, presenter Dallas Campbell reveals new scientific research and carries out unique experiments to get to the truth. For the first time, a virtual autopsy of Tut's mummified body reveals astonishing secrets about the pharaoh.

programme.title: Art That Made Us

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
